newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia may intervene in Bakun dam deadlock.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia may intervene in Bakun dam deadlock.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Thursday the government may intervene to resolve a dispute over the Bakun hydroelectric dam pact between the project's two key players.
He said there was also a remote possibility that the government would have to cancel the $5.5 billion contract, if the terms were found to be unfair.

Unresolved disagreements between Bakun's main developer Ekran Bhd and contractor ABB Asea Brown Boveri over some terms of the pact have led to government concerns that the $6.18 billion project may be delayed.
"They have been trying but they can't resolve. The next resort is the government will come in," Mahathir told reporters after lauching a go-kart event.
"If the worst comes to worst, and it is not possible to carry on, we may have to break the contract," he said.

"We can adhere to the contract if the terms are fair, but if they are shown to be grossly unfair, then we would have no choice. I do not know if it is grossly unfair or not. We will have to study," he added.
Ekran chairman Ting Pek Khiing said on Wednesday that the dispute was over terms that allowed the ABB-led consortium to claim cost overruns.

ABB and Brazil's Companhia Brasileria Projectos o Obras (CBPO) are co-heads of the consortium that was awarded the contract for the engineering, procurement and construction of the dam being built in Sarawak state on Borneo island.
A spokesman for ABB's office in Kuala Lumpur declined to comment on Thursday about the status of the contract. He said ABB and Ekran are meeting next week.
A prior meeting between ABB and Ekran on July 24 failed to resolve the differences, which are threatening to delay the dam, set to be completed by 2003.

ABB's portion of the work on Bakun includes supplying six 420 megawatt hydro-generators, a 500-kilovolt high voltage direct-current transmission system, installing a 650-km (400-mile) submarine cable to connect the dam to Peninsular Malaysia and civil engineering works with joint contractor CBPO.
Malaysia Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim who first brought up the issue two weeks ago said there were "major disagreements" in the pact which may delay the project's completion.
Some analysts said the delay could set back the listing of the project's operating company, Bakun Hydroelectric Corp Bhd (BHC).
BHC plans to issue 1.5 billion shares at two ringgit each.
